ordered_diagnoses: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration with motor neuron disease

facts.raw_span: 6-month history of progressive dysarthria and dysphagia
Family history notable for a relative with memory problems after age 80
Cognitive impairment
Vertical gaze palsy
Tongue atrophy
Pyramidal signs
Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia
Almost total loss in caudate nucleus
Left caudate: 0.35 (normal 1.55-2.07)
Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene (p.E643del) identified by whole-exon sequencing
Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies negative in serum and CSF
Large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potential in frontalis, mentalis, orbicularis oculi, and genioglossus muscles

rationales.F01: Progressive dysarthria and dysphagia are common in frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism-17 and frontotemporal lobar degeneration with motor neuron disease.
rationales.F04: Vertical gaze palsy is a characteristic feature of progressive supranuclear palsy.
rationales.F10: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene is a strong indicator of frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism-17.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, and tongue atrophy, along with the genetic testing showing a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, support the diagnosis of Frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism-17, which is a subtype of frontotemporal dementia associated with TBK1 mutations.
